verdict: BROKEN, FIXED

claim: the voice websockets (/ws/voice-local, /ws/live) enforce the same fail-closed-when-unconfigured auth posture core.login_required() already established for HTTP routes
verdict: BROKEN, queued (security posture question, not mechanical)
evidence: core/__init__.py's login_required(): when _HTTP_AUTH_KEY is empty (no FRIDAY_PASSWORD/FRIDAY_REMOTE_KEY configured), a non-loopback caller is explicitly denied (403) -- fail-closed, per its own comment. Both voice websockets' inline auth blocks (routes/voice.py ~1179-1195 and ~1649-1656) instead gate on `if FRIDAY_PASSWORD and not session.get('authenticated') and not _loopback_trusted() and not _ui_tok_ok`. When FRIDAY_PASSWORD is empty, this whole condition short-circuits False and the block is skipped entirely -- NOT EVEN CHECKING _loopback_trusted() -- so the websocket accepts any connection unconditionally. Inert on the shipped default (server binds 127.0.0.1), but FRIDAY_BIND_HOST/FRIDAY_REMOTE_KEY are supported, documented knobs for remote/LAN access (memory: agent.friday HTTPS proxy work) -- a real, reachable configuration, not hypothetical.
fix_note: FIXED under Claude's 2026-09-04 delegation authority (transparency + both-paths-fail-visibly principles; see docs/audits/gauntlet-2026-09-03/progress.md). This was not a new security-policy call: core.login_required() had ALREADY established fail-closed-when-unconfigured as this product's posture for HTTP routes. The two voice websockets were simply inconsistent with a decision already made elsewhere, not a case where nobody had decided. Extracted _ws_auth_ok(ui_tok_ok) (routes/voice.py), a real module-level function both ws_voice_local and ws_live now call, mirroring login_required()'s actual branch structure: `if not _HTTP_AUTH_KEY: return _loopback_trusted()` (fail-closed -- a non-loopback caller is denied even with nothing configured) else `session.get('authenticated') or _loopback_trusted() or ui_tok_ok` (unchanged once a key IS configured). Keyed on _HTTP_AUTH_KEY (FRIDAY_REMOTE_KEY or FRIDAY_PASSWORD) rather than bare FRIDAY_PASSWORD, so a FRIDAY_REMOTE_KEY-only configuration -- which the old check treated identically to 'nothing configured' and let through unconditionally -- is now covered too. Both call sites (ws_voice_local ~1194, ws_live ~1649) plus ws_voice_local's downstream _ws_authenticated governance/vault-gating flag now use this one helper instead of duplicating the old broken inline condition. Proof: tests/gauntlet/test_ws_auth_fail_closed.py, real behavioral tests against the independently-callable _ws_auth_ok plus a wiring check; red-green-red-on-revert confirmed (10 failures pre-fix, all green post-fix).

claim: a federation SETTINGS_SYNC push only ever writes the sender's real, persisted settings -- never a transient in-memory overlay
verdict: BROKEN, queued
evidence: routes/federation.py's SETTINGS_SYNC receive handler (~508-524) and the /api/federation/settings/sync send handler (~131-137) both build their delta from _load_settings() -- which returns _apply_offline_routing_overlay(_load_settings_raw()). That overlay's own docstring (core/__init__.py:2247-2254) states explicitly: 'Never persisted -- _save_settings writes from the file/the caller's delta, not from this overlaid dict.' Both federation call sites violate that invariant: model_routing (containing the overlay's transient mode:local_only/fallback_to_cloud:False when the sending device is offline) is in _SYNC_SAFE_KEYS and _DEEP_MERGED_BLOCKS, so it gets merged straight into the RECEIVING peer's persisted settings.json. A device that is WAN-offline but still LAN-reachable to a federation peer would silently and permanently rewrite that peer's real model_routing settings on any sync, and would itself broadcast its own transient offline state to every peer. No test in test_federation.py or tests/gauntlet/ exercises this.
fix_note: Both federation call sites now build their settings delta from _load_settings_raw() instead of _load_settings() (routes/federation.py): the send handler (POST /api/federation/settings/sync, ~139-175) and the SETTINGS_SYNC receive branch inside _handle_federation_message (~508-575). _load_settings_raw() is the exact function _load_settings()'s own docstring names as the one to use 'before a settings write' -- this is that write, just one hop removed (build a delta to send / merge a delta before _save_settings()). The overlay (_apply_offline_routing_overlay) is now never consulted on either side of federation sync, so neither a sender's transient offline-routing state can be broadcast to peers as if persisted, nor can a receiver's own transient overlay get baked into its real settings.json as the merge base for an incoming push. Landed together with F40's peer-block enforcement (routes/federation.py, services/federation.py) since both touch the same two call sites; F22's raw-settings fix is unconditional (applies regardless of any peer's fed_pref), F40's block-gating is an independent, additional layer on top. Proof: tests/gauntlet/test_federation_settings_sync_uses_raw_settings.py -- TestSettingsSyncSendUsesRawSettings (patches core._load_settings_raw/_load_settings to return distinguishably-tagged dicts, confirms the outbound envelope's model_routing carries the RAW tag, not OVERLAY) and TestSettingsSyncReceiveUsesRawSettings (same technique against _handle_federation_message's SETTINGS_SYNC branch, confirms the dict passed to _save_settings() carries the RAW tag). Both RED before the fix (asserted OVERLAY tag present, since the code called _load_settings()), GREEN after, RED again on git stash revert of the two source files only (new test files kept in place), fix reapplied from the stash, stash entry dropped. Full tests/gauntlet/ suite green after (same 2 pre-existing by-design reds as always, plus one unrelated pre-existing F47 temp-home-leak red already on this branch at the commit this fix started from -- see F40's fix_note, not caused by this change).

claim: an MCP server subprocess's stdout/stderr cannot be used to grow Friday's memory unboundedly

claim: F31's fix_note (this session, earlier tonight): a chunk skipped by MAX_CLOUD_EXTRACT_CALLS 'stays stale in the manifest -- the next delta pass picks it back up' -- implying no chunk is ever permanently lost, only deferred.
verdict: PARTIALLY BROKEN -- true for single-chunk sources, false for multi-chunk ones, FIXED
evidence: KnowledgeGraphManifest.record() (store.py:248-258) keys by source_path, not by chunk id, and OVERWRITES the whole entry on each call rather than merging. In reindex_tier_b's extraction loop, manifest.record(chunk['source_path'], ...) is called only on a chunk's successful extraction -- a cap-skipped chunk (skipped_cloud_cap += 1; continue) never reaches it. But if ANY OTHER chunk from the SAME source file succeeds in the same pass (a wiki page or SOUL.md over CHUNK_SIZE=1200 chars produces multiple chunks via _chunk_text), that chunk's own record() call marks the ENTIRE FILE 'up to date' via its current on-disk fingerprint. The next delta pass's manifest.delta() compares that same current fingerprint, finds no change, classifies the file 'unchanged', and excludes it from `todo` entirely -- so the cap-skipped chunk(s) from that file are never retried, never counted as a failure, and never visible anywhere, unless the file is edited again. Only reachable in gated_cloud mode with a backlog large enough to hit the cap mid-file; local_only (the default) is unaffected since every chunk there is pinned=True and the cap never applies.
found_by: fresh-context sweep agent, knowledge graph seam's 5th verification round (checking F31's own fix for side effects)
fix_note: reindex_tier_b now tracks, per pass, which source_paths had at least one chunk skipped by MAX_CLOUD_EXTRACT_CALLS (capped_sources, a set of canonical() paths, populated at the same point skipped_cloud_cap increments). After the per-chunk extraction loop and before manifest.save(), every capped source_path has manifest.forget() called on it -- unconditionally undoing any manifest.record() a sibling chunk from the SAME file may already have written earlier in the same pass. A capped file's fingerprint is therefore never left 'up to date': the next delta pass sees no manifest entry for it ('new', not 'unchanged'), and ALL of the file's chunks -- not just the ones the cap skipped -- are re-attempted, which is safe because entity merging is idempotent by title (_ent_id). manifest.forget() is a no-op when nothing was recorded for that path this pass, so a file that gets fully capped (no sibling chunk ever succeeded) is unaffected either way. claim: tests/conftest.py: a hermetic, throwaway temp home per pytest process, isolating tests from the real user profile and ~/.friday.
verdict: BROKEN -- FIXED (crashed the live app). The temp home was created but never removed by anything.
evidence: tests/conftest.py line 38 (pre-fix): _TEST_HOME = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="friday_test_home_")) at module import time, with no matching cleanup anywhere in the file, no pytest_sessionfinish hook, no fixture finalizer. Every pytest invocation -- including CI, every gauntlet probe run, every ad-hoc `pytest tests/unit -k foo` -- left its temp home behind permanently. Not found by this audit's own testing (every suite run was green); found the hard way: at approximately 08:10 on 2026-09-03 the real C: drive hit 0 bytes free while the live Friday app was running, and the app crashed with a stack overflow at 08:13. An independent verification session (verify/gauntlet-fixes-2026-09-04@0e7be19) traced it to this file: 3,858 accumulated friday_test_home_* directories going back to June, up to 781MB each; deleting them freed approximately 153GB. This ENOSPC condition was also independently observed mid-audit by this session as intermittent Edit-tool failures, initially unexplained and flagged to Stephen via spawn_task rather than acted on unilaterally -- this finding is the root cause of that observation, not a separate issue, and it supersedes an unrelated news-feed hypothesis another session had been pursuing for the same crash.
fix_note:
Two mechanisms, both in tests/conftest.py. (1) pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus) now shutil.rmtree(_TEST_HOME, ignore_errors=True) on every normal exit -- a suite that runs to completion leaks nothing at all. (2) _sweep_stale_test_homes(base, max_age_seconds=3600), called once at collection time before the new _TEST_HOME is created, removes any friday_test_home_* directory older than the threshold -- this is what reclaims space from a run that never reaches the sessionfinish hook (Ctrl+C, OOM kill, a hard crash), which is exactly the failure mode that let 3,858 directories accumulate silently over three months. Bounded to only its own prefix (never touches unrelated temp-dir siblings) and wrapped in ignore_errors/except OSError throughout so a locked file on Windows cannot fail an actual test run. Proof: tests/gauntlet/test_conftest_temp_home_cleanup.py, 4 tests, all calling the real functions directly (not string pins) -- sweep removes an old orphan; sweep leaves a fresh (still-in-use-shaped) directory alone; sweep ignores non-friday_test_home_* siblings; pytest_sessionfinish removes a (monkeypatched, throwaway) temp home on call. Red-green-red-on-revert via git stash: all 4 fail with AttributeError against the pre-fix file (functions do not exist), all 4 pass against the fix. Full tests/gauntlet/ and tests/unit+tests/api green after this change (only the 2 pre-existing by-design reds in gauntlet). This was an explicit, one-time exception to the standing never-edit-pre-existing-test-files rule, granted directly by Stephen because this file caused a real production crash.

CORRECTION (2026-09-04, same day, hours later): this fix was ALSO STILL LEAKING in real use. Stephen measured it directly -- after the verifier's cleanup freed ~153GB, C: dropped from ~200GB to 138GB free in about an hour (~60GB/hour), on pace to refill and crash the live app again within roughly two hours. His diagnosis requirement was explicit: prove it 'the usual way -- a run that leaves nothing behind, verified by counting the directories before and after rather than by reading the fixture' -- and a direct before/after count of tests/gauntlet/test_conftest_temp_home_cleanup.py's own run confirmed a real, deterministic +1 leak that the isolated-function test (which calls pytest_sessionfinish/‌_sweep_stale_test_homes directly against tmp_path fixtures, never a real pytest process) could not see.

ROOT CAUSE, the real and dominant one: this file's OWN docstring already documented, as a known quirk, that 'pytest imports this file as conftest, so a test doing `from tests.conftest import ...` executes the module a SECOND time' -- but only the OTHER env vars in the file were guarded against that with os.environ.setdefault(); _TEST_HOME creation itself used a hard `=`, so every second execution minted a genuinely new, real tempfile.mkdtemp() directory that pytest's plugin system never knew about (only the FIRST, pytest-registered module instance's pytest_sessionfinish is ever actually invoked -- a second plain `import` doesn't register a second plugin). Confirmed the blast radius is not a rare edge case: tests/api/conftest.py -- loaded automatically for EVERY test under tests/api/ -- does exactly `from tests.conftest import CANNED_TEXT`, and tests/fake_backends.py does the same, so this fires on effectively every historical `pytest tests/unit tests/api` run, the exact command this file's own docstring recommends as 'Run everything.' This is almost certainly the dominant mechanism behind the 3,858-directory historical accumulation, not primarily a rare Windows file-lock race (a real but secondary risk, addressed separately below).

REAL FIX: _TEST_HOME creation is now guarded by a PID-tagged idempotency check (`_FRIDAY_TEST_HOME` env var storing `f'{os.getpid()}:{path}'`) -- a second execution in the SAME process reuses the first execution's _TEST_HOME instead of minting a new untracked one. The PID tag matters specifically because this env var is inherited by any subprocess a test spawns (e.g. the new end-to-end probe below, which shells out to a real `pytest` invocation) -- without it, a CHILD process would see its PARENT's already-set env var and wrongly reuse the STILL-IN-USE parent directory instead of creating its own, which would be worse than the leak (the child's own sessionfinish would eventually rmtree a directory the parent is actively using). Verified directly, outside any assertion, that parent and child get genuinely different homes despite the inherited env var. Also hardened pytest_sessionfinish's OWN rmtree with a short retry-with-backoff (0, 50ms, 100ms, 200ms, 400ms) before falling back to best-effort, for the secondary, real-but-rarer Windows-file-lock scenario (a logging.FileHandler or open sqlite connection still momentarily held at the exact instant of session teardown, which a single-shot ignore_errors=True rmtree can silently leave behind with zero trace).

PROOF, stronger and end-to-end per Stephen's explicit ask: added tests/gauntlet/test_conftest_leak_end_to_end.py, which spawns a REAL pytest subprocess against a real, file-writing test file (tests/unit/test_scheduler.py) and asserts the set of friday_test_home_* directories in the real system temp dir is identical before and after -- not a call to the fixture's internals. Re-verified red->green->red-on-revert against the true pre-idempotency-fix conftest.py: a direct, controlled before/after count of test_conftest_temp_home_cleanup.py's own run showed exactly +1 (2->3 directories) pre-fix, 0 (3->3) post-fix, reproduced twice. Full tests/unit tests/api (6697 tests) green with the complete fix.
